title: Kyiv Faces Emergency Blackouts After Russian Strikes on Energy Grid
dek: Emergency power cuts hit Kyiv, the Kyiv region and Dnipro on Sunday after strikes that Zelenskyy said targeted substations tied to nuclear plants, with 600,000 customers reported without power in Dnipropetrovsk.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Flag map of Kherson, the Ukrainian city near the southern front where the localized ceasefire applies

keyPoints: Zelenskyy said Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles in a Nov. 7 attack aimed at Kyiv and the surrounding region, with the energy sector as the main target.
Zelenskyy said substations connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine were struck.
On Sunday, emergency power outages began in Kyiv, the Kyiv region and Dnipro, UA.NEWS reported, and hourly schedules were not in effect.
RFE/RL and UA.NEWS reported that 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region were without electricity; French officials said Paris would join U.S.-brokered talks on Nov. 10-11.
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia carried out a combined attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region on November 7, with strikes aimed at the country’s energy network. By Sunday, emergency blackouts were in effect in the capital and other cities.

## The November 7 attack

According to Zelenskyy, Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, and all the missiles were aimed at Kyiv and the surrounding region. He said residential buildings and the North Bridge were damaged, a kindergarten was partially destroyed, and nine people were injured, including one child. He said Russia also targeted twelve other regions.

## Nuclear plant substations

Zelenskyy said substations connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine were struck, and that substations were also damaged in the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipro regions. These are the president’s own damage claims; Meridian has not independently verified them.

## Sunday outages

On Sunday, Nov. 8, emergency power outages began in Kyiv, the Kyiv region and Dnipro, [UA.NEWS](https://ua.news/en/war-vs-rf/u-kiievi-kiyivskii-oblasti-ta-dnipri-zaprovadili-ekstreni-vidkliuchennia-svitla) reported, citing energy officials who said Ukrenergo directed the restrictions and that hourly schedules were not in effect. DTEK told customers not to rely on previously published schedules, according to UA.NEWS.

[RFE/RL](https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-strikes-ukraine-energy/33893219.html) reported that Russian attacks on the power system in Dnipropetrovsk region left 600,000 people without electricity. UA.NEWS, citing DTEK, reported the same 600,000-customer figure for that region. Dnipropetrovsk military chief Oleksandr Hanzha said hospitals had switched to diesel generators and electric-powered public transport had stopped in Dnipro, RFE/RL reported.

Zelenskyy said there were “widespread power outages across the country” and that in the Zhytomyr region alone, 140 apartment buildings were left without heating after a Russian strike, according to RFE/RL.

Ukrainian armed forces said Russia attacked overnight with three Kh-59/69 guided missiles and 164 strike drones, 137 of which were intercepted, RFE/RL reported. Ukrainian authorities said a strike in Dnipro killed one civilian and injured another, RFE/RL said. Battlefield claims have not been independently verified by Meridian.

## Repairs and equipment appeals

On Thursday, at a summit of the Ibero-American Community in Madrid, Zelenskyy said “every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged in one way or another by attacks,” and that repair crews were working around the clock. He asked Latin American and Spanish companies for help: “We need equipment that works with our power grid, and we need it fast,” the Guardian reported.

## Diplomacy

The Guardian reported that President Donald Trump predicted a “very big” deal with Russia that could involve more than Ukraine, after an unscheduled meeting with a Putin envoy. Trump said he had not met Ukrainian officials who were also at the White House that day. In the same statement on the grid attack, Zelenskyy said Kyiv is counting on increased bilateral support from the United States.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said France would take part in U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine peace talks on Nov. 10-11, RFE/RL reported. Barrot told RTL television that “the Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks.”

The Guardian reported that Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight airstrikes on Thursday, and that one of Russia’s largest oil refineries appeared to have come under attack. The paper said the strikes came as a second day of talks on Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction and security guarantees wrapped up in Brussels.

The Guardian also reported that a Ukrainian attack on a bus killed five people and wounded 13 in Ukraine’s Russian-occupied Luhansk region, according to the Moscow-backed leader there, Leonid Pasechnik. Those figures come from Pasechnik and have not been verified by Meridian.

Zelenskyy framed the November 7 attack as a sign that Moscow is preparing for trilateral negotiations by targeting critical infrastructure, according to UA.NEWS. That reading is the president’s own assessment and is presented here as his view, not as a verified finding.

## What we do not know

Meridian has not confirmed the full scale of Sunday outages, repair timelines, or any Russian response to the damage claims.
